# Themes

> Choose from five Paneflow palettes, switch between light and dark modes, or follow your system appearance. Changes apply without restarting.

Canonical: https://paneflow.dev/docs/themes

<!-- Auto-generated mirror of paneflow.dev - do not edit by hand.
     Source of truth: the paneflow.dev docs. Regenerated by
     scripts/sync-public-docs.ts in the site repo. -->

Choose a palette for Paneflow's terminals and interface, then select a
light, dark, or system appearance. Paneflow includes five palettes:
**Paneflow**, **Vercel**, **Claude**, **Cursor**, and **Tailwind**. Each
has a light and a dark variant. The default is **Paneflow Dark**.

Theme changes apply without restarting Paneflow, whether you use the
settings or edit `paneflow.json`.

## Choose a theme

1. Open **Appearance** in [Paneflow settings](/docs/settings).
2. Select **Light**, **Dark**, or **System**.
3. Choose a palette from **Preset**.

| Mode | Effect | Saved `theme_mode` value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Light | Use the light variant of the selected palette. | `"light"` |
| Dark | Use the dark variant of the selected palette. | `"dark"` |
| System | Follow your operating system's light or dark appearance. | `"system"` |

**System** remains selected after you close and reopen Paneflow. When
your system appearance changes, Paneflow switches variants while keeping
the same palette.

To return to **Paneflow Dark**, select **Reset to default** in the
**Theme** section.

## Included palettes

Use these exact names in the `theme` field of `paneflow.json`. Palette
names stay the same in every language.

| Preset | Light variant | Dark variant |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Paneflow | `Paneflow Light` | `Paneflow Dark` |
| Vercel | `Vercel Light` | `Vercel Dark` |
| Claude | `Claude Light` | `Claude Dark` |
| Cursor | `Cursor Light` | `Cursor Dark` |
| Tailwind | `Tailwind Light` | `Tailwind Dark` |

Names are case-insensitive. Older configurations still work: `One Dark`
resolves to `Paneflow Dark`, and `PaneFlow Light` resolves to
`Paneflow Light`. The old names `Vercel`, `Claude`, and `Cursor` resolve
to their dark variants.

## Set a theme in paneflow.json

Set `theme` to a variant from the table and `theme_mode` to the matching
mode. For example, to use Claude's light palette:

```paneflow.json
{
  "$schema": "https://github.com/arthjean/paneflow/raw/main/schemas/paneflow.schema.json",
  "$schemaVersion": "1.0.0",
  "theme": "Claude Light",
  "theme_mode": "light"
}
```

To follow your system appearance instead, set `theme_mode` to
`"system"`. Paneflow keeps the palette selected by `theme` and chooses
its light or dark variant to match your system.

The configuration file is stored at these default locations:

| System | Path |
| --- | --- |
| Linux and macOS | `~/.paneflow/paneflow.json` |
| Windows | `%USERPROFILE%\.paneflow\paneflow.json` |

If you set `PANEFLOW_HOME`, edit the file in that directory. See the
[configuration reference](/docs/configuration/schema) for all settings.

If `theme_mode` is omitted or `null`, Paneflow infers light or dark mode
from the theme name. To restore the default configuration, remove both
`theme` and `theme_mode`, or set both to `null`.

## What the theme changes

- Terminal background, text, cursor, selection, scrollbar, links, and ANSI colors.
- Interface backgrounds, borders, and text.
- Markdown panes and tables.
- Syntax colors in **Changes** and **Files**.

Some appearance settings are separate:

- `terminal.cursor_color` overrides the terminal cursor color. Set it to
  `null` to use the theme's cursor color.
- **Interface style** controls window materials and transparency. See
  [appearance settings](/docs/settings).
- `commands[].workspace.color` sets a workspace template's color.

## If the theme does not change

After editing `paneflow.json`, save the file. If the previous theme stays
visible, check that you edited the active configuration file and that
its JSON is valid. During reload, Paneflow keeps the previous valid
configuration if the new file contains a JSON error.

If you see **Paneflow Dark** instead of the palette you wanted, check
the theme name against the table above. An unknown name falls back to
Paneflow Dark and writes a warning to the logs.

For further checks, see [configuration troubleshooting](/docs/troubleshooting).
Changing `window_decorations` requires a restart, even though theme
changes do not.

## Custom palettes

Paneflow supports the bundled palettes only. It does not load
`theme.json` or custom palettes from `paneflow.json`.

To request another palette, [open a theme request on GitHub](https://github.com/arthjean/paneflow/issues)
and include the colors and how you would use them. To contribute a
bundled theme, start with `src-app/src/theme/builtin.rs` in the desktop
repository.
